narratives.Overview:
1. Keep envelope version `0.8`. Do not bump the envelope solely for reserved-prefix or clause:N compatibility.
2. Thread plan status into reserved-prefix severity. Change `validatePlanReferenceTypes` so it can take plan status (optional arg or options object). When status is omitted, keep today's CLASS_B-only severity so existing unit tests stay honest. When status is terminal (`completed` | `cancelled` | `failed`), unknown reserved-prefix subtypes MUST land in `warnings[]`, not `errors[]`. Call site in `validateVbriefSchema` already has `planObj.status` in scope and MUST pass it.
3. Do not treat `CLASS_B_COMPATIBILITY_BARES` membership as the durable compatibility product for this class. Reject shipping Visage by only appending its subtypes to CLASS_B as the primary fix. CLASS_B may remain as warning taxonomy for known corpora.
4. Leftover `clause:N` PlanItem ids on terminal plans: read-accept verbatim ids matching closed predicate `/^clause:[0-9]+$/` only (warn allowed; do not normalize in memory — edge resolution is exact-string). Thread the same terminal context through `validatePlanItem` recursively for `items` and `subItems`. Keep hard FAIL for other illegal ids on terminal, and for `clause:N` on non-terminal. Partial-migration edge mismatch (`clause.N` item + `clause:N` edge) is out of Prefer-A primary scope (leftover if observed).
5. Write-path co-acceptance: current leftover-complete / writers that mint PlanItem clause ids MUST emit `clause.N` only. Add an acceptance/test that current mint shape is dotted, so P2 does not recur on newly completed briefs after the read carve lands.
6. Warnings must not silently disappear. For the consumer validate CLI / `validate-all` path, warnings for these demoted classes MUST be collected and printed. Fixture acceptance MUST assert warning **presence** (and approximate count) for the demoted class, not only error absence. Document that `--warnings-as-errors` remains fail-closed (Visage default is non-strict). Optional aging/grandfather of permanent warn noise is a leftover, not a bind blocker for Visage's non-strict gate.
7. Normative fixture: a terminal (`completed`) brief carrying a **never-registered** reserved subtype (e.g. `x-xbrief/zz-never-registered-subtype`) plus `plan.items` id `clause:1` MUST produce 0 hard FAILs of class R (unknown reserved-prefix) and class C (clause-colon), AND must produce a warning for the unknown subtype. Visage vocabulary (`source-file` / `scope` / `artifact` / …) may land as a separate non-normative regression case. Include non-terminal control that still hard-FAILs unknown reserved-prefix outside CLASS_B, and malformed-id controls.
8. Acceptance wording: Prefer-A clears **0 errors of class R and class C** on terminal records / the normative fixture. Do not equate that with whole-corpus CLI exit 0. Before claiming a consumable npm cut for Visage, measure remaining validate errors by actual `plan.status` (not folder counts alone). Non-terminal class-R residue, if present and still blocking Visage's required gate, is either (a) folded by a Prefer-A Recut that extends warn demotion, or (b) a Tracking leftover with issue number — do not silently assert Visage can leave 0.119.2 from terminal-only clearance.
9. Explicit leftover (not Prefer-A primary): the one `failed` item missing `invalidates` edge on a completed plan; #1999 upgrade-rehearsal harness as release gate; #4749 Class A `pull-request` alias beyond terminal warn; #5385 Confidence enum; Claude C7 typo-distance option E + confusion matrix; C5 provenance-primary redesign; C6 aging channel.
10. Standing guard (C8 lite): under envelope 0.8, a regression test MUST fail closed if a future change reintroduces hard FAIL (`errors[]`) for an unknown reserved-prefix subtype on a terminal plan without an envelope-version bump. This is the machine form of acceptance bullet 4 for Prefer-A scope.

Reject B as primary: per-consumer CLASS_B growth is Stop 1 P3.
Reject C as primary: completed briefs are the record of what is (#3383).
Reject D as primary: envelope bump alone does not repair deposited 0.8 trees.

## Prefer-A draft (pre-Stop-1)

## In plain English
Visage (and any consumer with older completed xBRIEFs) cannot leave the 0.119.2 pin: every newer Directive cut hard-fails `vbrief:validate` on historical `x-xbrief/*` reference types Visage wrote under 0.119.2, plus leftover `clause:N` PlanItem ids, even though those files were never edited. Prefer-A keeps the 0.8 envelope, turns unknown reserved-prefix subtypes and leftover `clause:N` into warnings (not hard FAILs) on terminal briefs, keeps new writers on the canonical set / `clause.N`, ships a Visage-shaped fixture that must stay green of those two classes, and leaves per-consumer CLASS_B allowlist growth as a dead end for this compatibility class.

Open space (Stop 2 panel permission):
- A (Prefer-A): terminal-status warn/read-accept for unknown reserved-prefix + leftover clause:N; new writes stay canonical; Visage-shaped fixture; no envelope bump
- B: grow CLASS_B with every Visage subtype (repeats BlueLinx/BestiMax per-consumer cycle; next corpus fails again)
- C: require migrate/rewrite of completed history as the upgrade path (rejects completed-record freeze #3383)
- D: bump envelope to 0.9 for this class (larger blast; still leaves deposited 0.8 trees unreadable without migrate)

spend-recommend: N≥3
spend-why: genuinely open solution space (A/B/C/D) and high blast (required consumer validate gate + published npm cuts for every historical corpus)

## Bound remedy (draft limbs)
1. Keep envelope version `0.8`. Do not bump the envelope solely for reserved-prefix or clause:N compatibility.
2. In `validatePlanReferenceTypes` / `severityForUnknownReserved` (`packages/core/src/vbrief-validate/schema.ts`): when plan status is terminal (`completed` | `cancelled` | `failed`), unknown reserved-prefix subtypes (`x-xbrief/*` / `x-xbrief/*` outside STRICT/ENGINE/canonical) MUST land in `warnings[]`, not `errors[]`. Non-terminal statuses may keep today's hard FAIL for unknown subtypes outside CLASS_B. Thread plan status into the reference-type check (today `validatePlanReferenceTypes(references, filepath)` has no status discriminator).
3. Do not treat `CLASS_B_COMPATIBILITY_BARES` membership as the durable compatibility product for this class. CLASS_B may remain for warning taxonomy / known corpora; Prefer-A limb 2 is the upgrade-read path for terminal records. Do not ship Visage by only appending its subtypes to CLASS_B as the primary fix.
4. Leftover `clause:N` PlanItem ids: on the same terminal plan statuses, read-accept ids that fail `PLAN_ITEM_ID_PATTERN` solely because of a colon in the `clause:N` shape (warn allowed); keep hard FAIL for other illegal ids. New writers / leftover-complete on current engines MUST continue to mint `clause.N` only.
5. Checked-in fixture (Visage-shaped): a `completed/` (or equivalent test fixture) brief carrying at least `x-xbrief/source-file`, `scope`, `artifact`, and `plan.items` id `clause:1` MUST produce **0 hard FAILs** of the reserved-prefix-unknown and clause-colon classes under the shipped validator. Mirror any schema docs that would contradict that pass/fail.
6. Acceptance: public `@deftai/directive@` cut after this lands validates the Visage 0.119.2-valid corpus (or the checked-in fixture) with exit 0 for those two classes (warnings allowed); completed/cancelled briefs stay readable without rewrite; future reserved-prefix tightenings under the same 0.8 envelope cannot reintroduce hard FAILs on terminal records for unknown subtypes without an explicit migration/envelope change.
7. Out of Prefer-A primary scope (may leftover): wiring #1999 consumer upgrade-rehearsal harness as a release gate; expanding CLASS_B for non-terminal warn taxonomy; #4749 Class A `pull-request` alias remainder beyond terminal warn; #5385 Confidence enum (sibling landmine, separate corpus).

Reject B as primary: per-consumer CLASS_B growth is the failure mode that pinned Visage since 0.119.3.
Reject C as primary: completed briefs are the record of what is (#3383); rewrite is not a supported upgrade path.
Reject D as primary: envelope bump alone does not make already-deposited 0.8 trees readable and widens blast.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

Consumer **deftai/deftvisage** has been stuck on an exact `@deftai/directive@0.119.2` family since `validatePlanReferenceTypes` landed in 0.119.3. Every later public npm cut we have tried — 0.119.6 through 0.119.13, 0.120.0, and **0.121.0 today** — fails `vbrief:validate` on unchanged historical xBRIEFs. Visage 4.9.170 (2026-10-06) still pins `tools/deft-cli` at `^0.119.2` and CI installs that exact family from registry.npmjs.org.

This is a consumer hard-stop: the DEFT/vBRIEF CI job is a required gate. There is no reasonable workaround that preserves completed/cancelled history.

Title token: `BLOCKER`. That token does not apply the `adoption-blocker` ranking label.

## Why this keeps happening on every npm update

The failure is not a Visage product regression and it is not the 0.121.0 `narratives.Confidence` enum change (#5385). Visage's corpus has **no** `plan.narratives.Confidence` fields.

What repeats:

1. **0.119.3 introduced a closed reserved-prefix registry** (`validatePlanReferenceTypes` in `@deftai/directive-core`, for #4698 / #4746). Schema still accepts namespaced `x-xbrief/*` strings. Runtime then fail-closes any reserved subtype that is missing from three lists:
   - `STRICT_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST` / `KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES`
   - `ENGINE_WRITTEN_BARE_TYPES`
   - `CLASS_B_COMPATIBILITY_BARES` (warning-only membership)
2. **Compatibility has been grown per filing consumer**, not by accepting historical `x-xbrief/*` as readable 0.8 data:
   - #4746 / #4765 added BlueLinx bares (`depends-on`, `supersedes`, `source-document`, …).
   - #4846 added nine BestiMax bares (`prerequisite`, `related-pr`, `source`, `origin`, …).
   - Visage's vocabulary was never added. `x-xbrief/source` is now a **warning** (BestiMax overlap). `x-xbrief/source-file`, `scope`, `artifact`, `doc`, `sibling`, `pr`, … remain **errors**.
3. **Completed xBRIEFs are the record of what is** (#3383). They still carry the types the 0.119.2 writer emitted. Each `npm i @deftai/directive@latest` re-validates that frozen history against the latest closed set and exits 1. The Visage pin is rolled back, the changelog notes the failure, and the next release tries again.
4. **A second fail-closed class is leftover `clause:N` PlanItem ids.** `PLAN_ITEM_ID_PATTERN` is `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)*$`, so a colon is illegal. #5011 shipped a `clause:N` → `clause.N` migrator; Visage cannot run a rewrite of completed history as the upgrade path. `leftover-complete` on the 0.119.2 family still mints `clause:1` into completed briefs (example: `xbrief/completed/2026-10-05-fix-2011-consult-tile-still.xbrief.json`, `recorded_by: leftover-complete`).

So an npm update of Directive looks like: install latest → `task vbrief:validate` / `deft vbrief:validate` → 274 hard FAILs on files nobody edited → revert to 0.119.2. That loop has been running on Visage for dozens of patch cuts.

## Expected behavior

A supported consumer upgrade from an exact 0.119.2 family to 0.121.0 preserves validation of previously accepted 0.8 xBRIEFs, including completed and cancelled records, without hand-rewriting historical reference types or `clause:N` ids.

## Actual behavior

Same Visage tree, isolated public-npm installs, Node v24.14.0, 2026-10-06:

| Engine | `vbrief:validate --project-root <visage>` |
|---|---|
| exact 0.119.2 family (`directive` + `directive-core` + `content` + `types`) | **exit 0** — 653 scope vBRIEFs, 16 pre-existing warnings (D11 / timestamp) |
| 0.121.0 (`@deftai/directive@0.121.0` → core/content 0.121.0) | **exit 1** — **274 errors**, 300 warnings |

### Error classes under 0.121.0 (274)

**195 unknown reserved-prefix subtype errors** (15 types), 222 of 274 FAILs sit in `xbrief/completed/`:

| Count | Type | Notes |
|---:|---|---|
| 103 | `x-xbrief/source-file` | Dominant Visage type; not in CLASS_B |
| 30 | `x-xbrief/scope` | |
| 29 | `x-xbrief/artifact` | |
| 6 | `x-xbrief/sibling` | |
| 5 | `x-xbrief/doc` | |
| 5 | `x-xbrief/dependency` | |
| 4 | `x-xbrief/design-reference` | |
| 3 | `x-xbrief/probe` | |
| 3 | `x-xbrief/pr` | Alias map only has `pull-request` / `github-pull-request` → `github-pr` |
| 2 | `x-xbrief/split-child` | |
| 1 each | `x-xbrief/design-doc`, `related-vbrief`, `code`, `pull-request`, `strategy` | `pull-request` is the #4749 Class A remainder |

**78 `plan.items[clause:N] invalid id` errors** (colon vs `PLAN_ITEM_ID_PATTERN`).

**1** unrelated `failed` item missing `invalidates` edge.

Warnings that are **not** the blocker: 281× `x-xbrief/source` (CLASS_B), 2× `x-xbrief/depends-on`, 1× `x-xbrief/origin`, plus the same timestamp/D11 warnings 0.119.2 already printed.

Sample reserved-prefix FAIL:

```
FAIL: xbrief/cancelled/2026-05-11-feat-consolidate-popup-project-chat.xbrief.json: plan.references[0].type 'x-xbrief/source-file' is an unknown reserved-prefix subtype
```

Sample clause FAIL (completed, minted by leftover-complete):

```
FAIL: xbrief/completed/2026-10-05-fix-2011-consult-tile-still.xbrief.json: plan.items[clause:1] invalid id: 'clause:1'
```

## Steps to reproduce

From a deftai/deftvisage checkout (no repo edits):

```sh
npm install --prefix /tmp/deft-cli-0.119.2 --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund \
  --registry https://registry.npmjs.org \
  @deftai/directive@0.119.2 @deftai/directive-core@0.119.2 \
  @deftai/directive-content@0.119.2 @deftai/directive-types@0.119.2

npm install --prefix /tmp/deft-cli-0.121.0 --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund \
  --registry https://registry.npmjs.org \
  @deftai/directive@0.121.0

node /tmp/deft-cli-0.119.2/node_modules/@deftai/directive/dist/bin.js \
  vbrief:validate --project-root "$PWD"
# exit 0

node /tmp/deft-cli-0.121.0/node_modules/@deftai/directive/dist/bin.js \
  vbrief:validate --project-root "$PWD"
# exit 1, 274 errors
```

Minimal structural fixture for the reserved-prefix class (same shape as #4846):

```json
{
  "xBRIEFInfo": { "version": "0.8" },
  "plan": {
    "title": "Visage reserved-prefix compatibility",
    "status": "completed",
    "items": [],
    "references": [
      { "uri": "src/preview/web-app-preview-pipeline.ts", "type": "x-xbrief/source-file" }
    ]
  }
}
```

This is valid under core 0.119.2 and one unknown-reserved-prefix **error** under core 0.121.0. Substitute `x-xbrief/scope`, `artifact`, `doc`, `sibling`, `pr`.

## Consumer impact

- **Repo:** https://github.com/deftai/deftvisage
- **Pin:** `tools/deft-cli/package.json` → `"@deftai/directive": "^0.119.2"` with lockfile resolved to 0.119.2 for directive, core, content, and types (public npm tarballs).
- **CI:** required job `DEFT/vBRIEF validation` installs `@deftai/directive@${DEFT_VER}` **and** `@deftai/directive-core@${DEFT_VER}` from registry.npmjs.org. Comment in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: *Pin to tools/deft-cli, not @latest … 0.119.3 reserved-prefix fails historical xBRIEFs.* A caret install of 0.119.2 alone can float a newer core (#4846 / #4766).
- **Release habit:** each Visage patch (through 4.9.170) tries public latest, records the same validate failure in CHANGELOG, keeps the pin.
- Rewriting 125 historical files (222 completed FAILs) is not a supported upgrade path.

## Proposed next steps

The CLASS_B allowlist-per-corpus strategy will keep failing the next consumer. A durable 0.8 read path:

- Unknown reserved-prefix subtypes on existing 0.8 documents (at least terminal `completed` / `cancelled` / `failed`) go to **warnings**, not `errors[]`. New writers can keep emitting the canonical set.
- Read-accept leftover `clause:N` PlanItem ids on those same records; keep new writes on `clause.N`. Validate must not require `migrate:xbrief` to keep history readable.
- Stop treating `CLASS_B_COMPATIBILITY_BARES` membership as the compatibility product. A checked-in Visage-shaped fixture (`source-file` / `scope` / `artifact` / `clause:1` under `completed/`) should stay 0 hard FAILs of these two classes on the next publish.
- Run the existing consumer upgrade-rehearsal idea (#1999) against a real historical corpus before cutting npm.

Do not recut #4698 into pattern-only silent acceptance of typos. Do not require `verify:orphan-active` changes. Do not treat this as #5385 (Confidence enum); link it as a sibling 0.121.0 upgrade landmine.

## Related

- #4746 (closed) — 0.119.3 BlueLinx reserved-prefix BLOCKER
- #4749 (open) — Class A `pull-request` alias remainder; Visage has one `x-xbrief/pull-request`
- #4765 (closed) — BlueLinx unenumerated 20
- #4846 (closed) — BestiMax nine types; same mechanism, different vocabulary
- #5011 (closed) — `clause:N` id pattern + migrator; leftover ids still fail-close
- #5385 (open) — 0.121.0 Confidence enum; **not** this corpus
- #4698 (closed) — pattern vs closed-set consumption
- #1999 (open) — consumer-side upgrade rehearsal harness
- Visage pin / 4.9.170: https://github.com/deftai/deftvisage (CHANGELOG 4.9.170 “Deft CLI”)

## Environment

- Consumer: deftai/deftvisage @ 4.9.170 / origin/main
- Host: macOS, Node v24.14.0
- Public npm `@deftai/directive@0.119.2` (exact family) vs `@deftai/directive@0.121.0`
- Gate: `deft vbrief:validate` / Visage `task vbrief:validate` (required CI)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Exact 0.119.2-valid Visage corpus (or the checked-in fixture) exits 0 on 0.121.x+ for the reserved-prefix and `clause:N` classes above, with warnings allowed.
- [ ] Completed/cancelled briefs stay readable without rewrite.
- [ ] A published npm cut exists that Visage can take without remaining on 0.119.2.
- [ ] Future reserved-prefix tightenings cannot ship as hard FAILs under the same 0.8 envelope with no migration / no warning channel.
